note: Written BEFORE any LAB-07 code. Every clause of the LAB-07 tasks, guide 9.5 (campaign/bank migration), guide 10.3 (one economic engine and account path), the acceptance requirements LAB-07 owns (T53-T57) and the phase outputs and exit gate. scripts/audit_lab07.py reads THIS file, so the audit cannot become a list of what happened to get built.
clauses: with the experimental scheduler and regime provider DISABLED, the continuous run reproduces the current canonical baseline path exactly: same orders
disabled-hooks parity also holds for the account path (cash, position, equity), not only for orders
disabled-hooks parity also holds for reported metrics
disabled-hooks parity also holds for selection: the same candidate is chosen at every cutoff
the same FIXED intents replay identically on the Python and the Rust backend, and this parity is established BEFORE any performance claim
a hook that is enabled but makes no decision must still not change the baseline path; 'disabled' and 'enabled but inert' are tested separately
one ordered event stream carries market bar completions
the same stream carries regime-ready observations
the same stream carries refit REQUEST, START and READY as three distinct events
the same stream carries parameter activations
the same stream carries engine fills
the event clock breaks ties with a sequence id, never with millisecond equality
the engine can never read a future activation_end; an activation's end is unknown until the next activation exists
an event whose available_at is later than the current clock is not visible, even if its observed_at is in the past
a refit's candidate evaluation runs under its OWN account policy (normally flat/reset for training)
a refit never mutates the continuous deployment account
a refit job cannot access any data after its request cutoff
refit latency comes from a measured benchmark, the resource budget, or a frozen scenario
a refit latency of zero is never used in order to fill earlier (guide L07.3 names this explicitly)
the training account contract is recorded and is NOT identified with the deployment account contract (guide 10.3)
an entry campaign carries an immutable entry_parameter_digest
when the regime changes, an OPEN trade stays protected by the parameters it entered with
pending future-entry policy MAY change while an open campaign keeps its own
pending entry commands have explicit cancel/retain semantics at an activation
an old campaign's protective orders keep their parameter version until terminal
retired parameter versions are never deleted while an order still references them
new candidate indicators must be causally warm before activation; wait or fall back rather than reinitialise
no EMA/HMA reset at a switch, and no adaptive-length state carried from params A to params B without a declared contract
activation records both the requested decision time and the ACTUAL activation delay
bank switching uses the same QuantBT order lifecycle as any other order; no side channel
a campaign that will not close is reported stale/transition-blocked; it is never force-closed to manufacture a timing edge
forced unwind exists only as a separate ablation and carries its costs
a segment STARTS when its parameters become effective
a segment's END is only written once a NEXT activation exists; the open segment has a null end
a trigger may legitimately result in no change; a no-change trigger is recorded, not dropped
the reporting clock is unchanged by segmentation: daily UTC on one evaluation interval
no future segment length ever enters a policy decision
segments of different length are never averaged as unweighted fold Sharpes to rank arms (T55)
stale context is handled explicitly and is distinguished from missing
a failed model fit keeps the validated incumbent; it never selects random parameters
an incomplete probe panel is incomplete evidence, not bad performance
an out-of-order job completion cannot activate earlier than its READY event
a simulation reject is handled and recorded
a liquidation is handled and recorded
an interrupted artifact write is detected; a partial artifact is never read as complete
a worker failure does not erase already-committed trials
feeding one observation/event at a time gives exactly the offline event replay under the same availability
mutating the future does not change any past decision
reset/resume is offered ONLY if a full model+strategy+account state contract supports it; otherwise it is refused, not approximated
the prefix of a longer stream equals the whole of the shorter stream, for decisions and for the account
each arm has its own account with the SAME initial conditions
within an arm the account is continuous in chronological order
best segments from independent runs are never summed (T56)
money is never reset at a regime or fold change (T56)
fees, slippage, funding and gross exposure constraints are identical across arms
A/B/C/D share fixed economics and budgets with no hidden fee, risk or evaluation advantage
an installed WFO mode that uses OOS for selection is reported as A_legacy_selection_adjusted, never as an untouched baseline
dynamic folds of different length are compared on the same daily account, not by averaging fold Sharpes
a carried account across segments shows no reset and no virtual splice of expert PnL
a sequential optimizer and an adaptive batch are declared as different contracts; no false identical-sequence claim
a lab-only QuantBT patch/diff exists as a PROPOSAL and is never applied upstream
integration_binding_map.json maps each lab integration point to a VERIFIED installed symbol
regime provider, scheduler and parameter-provider adapters exist
installed-lab smoke tests run against the INSTALLED package, not a mock
no leakage: every causality probe passes and the leaky control is still detected
no account resets anywhere in a continuous arm
no handcrafted fills: every fill comes from the engine
an unsupported hook is a BLOCKER or a documented lab patch; it is never silently routed to a different contract
